units.text: Debugging UI tests often requires inspecting the screen state and composition hierarchy when an assertion fails. Compose provides a native failure handling pipeline to streamline diagnostics. You can automatically capture screenshots and UI hierarchies upon failure, or register custom handlers to forward crash telemetry to external tools.

quotes.quote: Debugging UI tests often requires inspecting the screen state and composition hierarchy when an assertion fails.

Compose provides a native failure handling pipeline to streamline diagnostics. You can automatically capture screenshots and UI hierarchies upon failure, or register custom handlers to forward crash telemetry to external tools.

units.text: To configure failure handling, pass a `TestFailurePolicy` object to `ComposeUiTestConfig`. To capture screenshots and UI hierarchies upon test failure, set the `screenshotCaptureMode` and `uiHierarchyCaptureMode` properties in `TestFailurePolicy`.

units.text: To define custom behavior for test failures, add a `TestFailureHandler` to the `failureHandlers` list. Each handler receives a `FailureContext` object that contains the original error and a list of artifacts generated by the preceding pipeline handlers.

units.text: Starting with Robolectric 4.15, it's possible to launch an interactive preview of your app or tests in a Robolectric environment. The Robolectric simulator can be a useful way to preview how your UI would look in a Robolectric environment. This can be helpful, for instance, when debugging failing Robolectric tests.

units.text: Note that the Robolectric simulator is highly experimental and is still largely in the proof-of-concept stage. UI rendered in the Robolectric simulator may not match an Android emulator or device 100%.

units.text: There are two ways to launch the simulator: with the simulator Gradle plugin or by invoking the simulator APIs from tests.

units.text: To enable the Robolectric simulator with the Gradle plugin, add the plugin to the plugins block of your app's `build.gradle`/`build.gradle.kts` file:

units.text: id("org.robolectric.simulator") version "1.0.3"

quotes.quote: id("org.robolectric.simulator") version "1.0.3"

units.text: Then, run `./gradlew simulate<variant>` (for example, `./gradlew simulateDebug` or `./gradlew simulateDemoDebug`) to start the simulator for the `<variant>` build variant. It will run the main Activity that is configured in your manifest.

units.text: To enable the simulator to work with JDK 23 and newer, you must add the following extra jvmArgs to your unit test configuration:

quotes.quote: To enable the simulator to work with JDK 23 and newer, you must add the following extra jvmArgs to your unit test configuration:

testOptions { unitTests { all { test -> test.jvmArgs( "--add-exports=java.desktop/sun.awt=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-exports=java.base/sun.reflect.misc=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-exports=java.base/sun.security.action=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-exports=java.desktop/sun.swing=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-exports=java.desktop/sun.lwawt.macosx=ALL-UNNAMED", ) } } }

units.text: If your tests fail after upgrading to v2, they likely exhibit the following pattern:

quotes.quote: If your tests fail after upgrading to v2, they likely exhibit the following pattern:

units.text: - Failure: You launch a task (for example, a ViewModel loads data), but your assertion fails immediately because the data is still in a "Loading" state.

units.text: - Cause: With the v2 APIs, coroutines are queued rather than executed immediately. The task was queued but never actually ran before the result was checked.

quotes.quote: Cause: With the v2 APIs, coroutines are queued rather than executed immediately. The task was queued but never actually ran before the result was checked.

units.text: - Fix: Explicitly advance time. You must explicitly tell the v2 dispatcher when to execute work.

quotes.quote: Fix: Explicitly advance time. You must explicitly tell the v2 dispatcher when to execute work.
